Login protectionMoodle 4.1+

Brute Force Detect

Stop repeated password guesses without blocking an entire campus after a few mistakes.

Brute Force Detect protects regular Moodle sign-ins and web-service login requests. Administrators set separate limits for attempts against one account and for attempts coming from the same IP address, helping balance security with everyday access.

Protection administrators control
  • Attempts per username and IP address.
  • Broader limits for shared network IP addresses.
  • Tracking window and temporary block duration.
  • Automatic removal of expired counters.
Focused account protection
Repeated failed attempts against the same account can be temporarily blocked without automatically restricting every other user on that network.
Shared-network awareness
A separate overall IP threshold gives institutions flexibility when students or staff use a common public address.
Existing-site migration
Sites moving from the older Brute Force authentication plugin can retain useful protection settings and recent attempt information.
Why use two different limits?

A campus, school or company may have hundreds of legitimate users behind one public IP address. A very low shared-IP limit can prevent everyone from signing in because one person entered the wrong password several times.

Brute Force Detect distinguishes focused attempts against an account from larger patterns across an address. Successful sign-ins clear the relevant account-focused counter, while expired restrictions end automatically.

Privacy and operations: IP addresses are retained temporarily for protection, while usernames are not stored in plain text in account-focused counters. Review thresholds for your site's traffic and keep Moodle scheduled tasks running.
